governance: Independently governed expected magnitudes for the model router (maistro-core/router + its two RoutingConfig copies). This file states the values the implementation must produce; it is NOT generated from or imported by production code, so a mutation of a production constant cannot silently rewrite its own expectation. Changing a value here is a routing-policy change: it needs the same review as changing the production constant, plus the cited provenance updated in lockstep.

routing.default_weights.source: packages/maistro-core/src/maistro/types/config.py:14-16 AND packages/maistro-core/src/maistro/config/settings.py:310-312 (two copies that must stay identical)
routing.default_weights.provenance: shipped routing policy: quality-dominant with a real cost trade-off (score = quality^(qw*p) / (1+norm_cost)^cw); reserve_pct is the quota band held back from non-P0 traffic (filter.py)
routing.default_weights.protects: which model serves production traffic: quality_weight/cost_weight set how hard cost pushes against quality; doubling quality_weight (0.6->1.2) makes every cheap-provider tier collapse onto quality ordering, halving cost_weight (0.4->0.2) halves the 2x-at-cw=1.0 cheap/expensive spread; doubling reserve_pct starves non-P0 traffic of 10% of quota
routing.default_weights.kills: any mutation of either copy, and any drift between the two copies (types/config.py vs config/settings.py)

routing.default_priority_multipliers.provenance: priority escalation of the quality exponent (quality^(qw * mult)): P0 gets the steepest quality push, P5 the gentlest; P2 is the neutral 1.0 anchor
routing.default_priority_multipliers.protects: urgent traffic earns stronger quality preference: P0=1.5 vs P2=1.0 at quality 0.9/qw 0.6 is a 0.9^0.3 (~7%) score edge; flattening the ladder (P0->1.0) silently removes priority routing, steepening it (P0->3.0) makes priority dominate cost entirely
routing.default_priority_multipliers.kills: any mutated multiplier in either copy, and drift between the copies

speed.SPEED_WEIGHTS.provenance: task-type speed policy: automation (voice) 0.25 fast-response-critical, chat 0.15, code/reasoning 0.0 quality-is-everything; module docstring states the same ladder
speed.SPEED_WEIGHTS.protects: latency vs quality per task type: adjusted_quality = quality * (1 + weight * norm_speed); doubling automation to 0.5 lets a 2000-token/s low-quality model outscore a 0.3-better model in voice routing
speed.SPEED_WEIGHTS.kills: any mutated weight, including 0.0 -> non-zero for code/reasoning (quality-is-everything) and reordering (automation must exceed chat)

speed._MAX_SPEED.provenance: speed normalisation anchor: norm_speed = min(1, speed/_MAX_SPEED) — the tokens/s that earns the FULL speed bonus
speed._MAX_SPEED.protects: how fast a model must be to saturate the speed bonus; doubling to 4000 halves every model's speed bonus, halving to 1000 lets mediocre models saturate it
speed._MAX_SPEED.kills: any magnitude mutation of the anchor (calibration: bonus at 2000 tok/s is exactly the task weight, at 1000 exactly half)

scorer.cost_band.provenance: the realistic scarcity-cost band (1B-token budget barely used -> 10k budget at 99% consumed) the normalizer maps onto [0,1]; the old theoretical ceiling 1/ln(2) compressed every realistic cost to [0.03,0.15] and capped the cost term at ~10% of the score even at cost_weight=1.0 (repo-history task, measured 2026-07)
scorer.cost_band.protects: the contract that at cost_weight=1.0 a fresh huge-budget provider genuinely scores ~2x a nearly-exhausted small one; the band endpoints decide WHICH raw costs count as cheapest and most expensive
scorer.cost_band.kills: mutating 1e9->1e6 or 100->10 in the band formulas (derivation check: floor == 1/ln(1e9), ceil == 1/ln(100)) and any magnitude change of the in-budget cap

scorer.strength_mult.provenance: matched preferred-strength bonus: quality * 1.15 when the model's declared strengths intersect the intent's; the old 0.90 PENALTY for unmatched strengths made deleting the metadata field optimal
scorer.strength_mult.protects: metadata presence must pay, slightly: a matched strength is a 15% quality edge — big enough to matter, small enough not to beat a genuinely better model; 1.15 -> 1.5 makes strength labels dominate real quality
scorer.strength_mult.kills: any magnitude mutation (calibration: quality 0.8 with a matched strength scores exactly 0.92)

scarcity.OVER_QUOTA_FLOOR.provenance: anchor just above the theoretical in-budget ceiling 1/ln(2): paid overage starts strictly above every free in-budget cost so free quota always wins while paygo stays rankable
scarcity.OVER_QUOTA_FLOOR.protects: free in-budget quota always beats paid overage on the router's cost-in-denominator score; lowering the floor below the in-budget band makes the router PREFER paying
scarcity.OVER_QUOTA_FLOOR.kills: any mutation of the floor (derivation check: floor == 1/ln(2) + 1, and floor > scorer._RAW_CEIL strictly)

scarcity.INELIGIBLE_COST.provenance: sentinel returned for over-quota-without-paygo providers; the scorer FILTERS on it (returns None) rather than scoring it
scarcity.INELIGIBLE_COST.protects: a provider with no quota and no paygo is never selected; a sentinel inside the realistic band would let an unusable provider win on cheapness
scarcity.INELIGIBLE_COST.kills: any magnitude mutation (999 -> 9.99 would collide with the normalized paygo band and break the filter's shared-constant contract with scorer.py)
